title: The best thing I invested in when I was pregnant
body:
I chose to invest in Tiny Hearts courses instead of spending money on fancy baby clothes or nursery gadgets, and it was one of the best decisions we've made as parents. To be honest, while learning those skills, we hope we’d never need them. You can never predict what challenges your child might face, but you can prepare yourself to respond.

Our twins are now 2 years old, and I've honestly lost count of how many times the knowledge from these courses has helped us recognise when something wasn't right, know what to do while seeking medical care, and confidently advocate for our children.

We've dealt with breastmilk aspiration, multiple episodes of respiratory distress from RSV, rhinovirus and other viral infections, managed febrile seizures, and we're now navigating our daughter's ultra-rare genetic condition. Throughout all of these experiences, the education from Tiny Hearts has given us the confidence to stay calm, ask the right questions, and make informed decisions.

On more than one occasion, doctors and nurses have commented on how proactive we are and have even asked whether we have a medical background because of the questions we ask and the observations we make.

Tiny Hearts courses have been worth every single dollar and we recommend it for every new family we know.
productName: Online Baby & Child First Aid Course: Australia
reply: Flavia, thank you so much for this incredibly heartfelt review! 💛 We are truly moved by your story and so grateful you chose to invest in your family's safety with Tiny Hearts. Reading about everything you and your twins have been through, and knowing that the knowledge from our courses helped you stay calm, advocate for your children and make informed decisions through it all, means the absolute world to us. 🥹 The fact that doctors and nurses have noticed how prepared and proactive you are is just so amazing and you should be so proud of yourselves! That is exactly why we do what we do. 🙌 Thank you for recommending us to every new family you know. It genuinely takes a village and you are helping to make more families safer. We are cheering your beautiful little family on every step of the way! 💕

title: Cold packs are insufficient
body: I found the breast cold packs to be very thin and therefore don’t get that cold at all and very quickly become warm once they are on you, therefore not working.
reply:
Hi Sally,

Thank you so much for taking the time to share this with us. I'm really sorry to hear the breast cold packs didn’t meet your expectations, especially during such a tender recovery period when comfort makes such a difference.

I know how important that cooling relief can be in those early days, so I completely understand how disappointing it would feel if they weren’t as cold or long-lasting as you’d hoped.

They’re intentionally designed to be softer and more flexible so they sit gently against sensitive skin, which can make them feel thinner than traditional gel packs. For the best cooling effect, we recommend chilling them flat for several hours (or keeping a second pair in the fridge/freezer to rotate between uses).

We truly appreciate you sharing your experience, feedback like this helps us continue refining our products to better support our Tiny Hearts mums.

Wishing you a smooth and gentle recovery.

Warmly,
Nikki xx

We had a private Tiny Hearts course and honestly… 10/10, no notes. Ellie was an absolute legend – super informative, calm, and somehow managed to teach us essential first aid while we juggled babies, dogs, snacks, and the occasional nappy change.

She created such a relaxed and welcoming vibe that we forgot we were learning about scary stuff – we just left feeling confident and informed. Highly recommend for any new parents wanting practical, clear info delivered in a setting that feels like a catch-up with friends (who just happen to be learning to save lives).

Thanks Ellie – you nailed it!

Hi Kate,

That's an absolutely glowing review! I am so incredibly thrilled to hear about your outstanding Private Tiny Hearts Course experience.

Ellie truly is an absolute legend, and I am delighted she created such a relaxed, informative, and welcoming vibe for you, even with all the joys of juggling babies, dogs, and snacks! Her ability to make learning essential first aid feel like a catch-up with friends, while still instilling such confidence, is exactly what we strive for.

I've shared your feedback with our team so we can look at how to improve this experience moving forward.

Your suggestions around the product mix are also really helpful. We’re always reviewing the balance of items in the kit, and insights like yours are key to helping us make it even better for new mums.

Thanks again for your honesty and for helping us grow.

body:
After having my second son, I was really worried about choking and just had this instinct that kept coming up telling me to do a first aid course. I kept putting it off. But I follow your page and watch all your videos on what to do. My son started solids and was at a stage we could give him banana, sliced long ways not in circles and I had read somewhere to roll it in coconut to help for grip. He’d had this many of times. But one day, my partner has OMG he’s choking. Usually it’s just gagging but this time there was no noise. I ripped him out of his chair and immediately administered back blows. After just a few, the banana dislodged. That very week I told my beauty therapist and said I was going to do a Tiny Hearts online course when she said ‘no way I’ve wanting to do one, let’s organised a private group one’ and that’s just what we did. I have since referred back to your take home book for various things just for extra reassurance that my babies are okay. 
Usually I would panic, but I remained so calm when my son really needed me. Afterwards I was in shock how quickly things had changed but I was also so glad I knew who to do and how to do it calmly.

Thank you for choosing Tiny Hearts to empower you, I'm so grateful to have you as part of our community.

title: Amazing course
body:
Absolutely amazing. 

I was eating lunch out at a restaurant with my 3 year old, 6 month old, partner and my Dad who was visiting us at the time. My 6 month old was interested in my hot chips so I placed her in the high chair and gave her a cooled hot chip to suck / chew on. It was going fine, until it wasn’t. I watched her drop some of the chip while a larger piece went into her mouth, I looked at my partner and said worryingly, oh god I think she could choke on this… he said stick your finger in her mouth and get it out if your worried and I replied with no, that could make it worse we just need to play this out and see how she goes. It felt like within 10 seconds of me saying this, she started to choke. I could see the expression in her face, I unbuckled her out of her high chair, gave her 2 back blows and out came this piece of hot chip. 

My partner (her dad) and my dad both clapped and said they could not have done that any better or quicker and were quite stunned with my quick reaction.

My heart was beating out of my chest, but I know I responded and did what I done and saved my daughter’s life because of this course so thank you.

All for inclusion but this was difficult to see the value of given the technique was so difficult to work out. Also, would have been good if there was a table at the front so that people outside of the front row could see the live demonstrations that the trainer had to do on the dolls on the floor.  Didnt seem to make sense that there wasnt something higher than the ground for the demo to be done on. I didnt want to stand up to block the people behind me so missed a bit of content on that.

Overall - I still found it informative given that my knowledge base on this, especially with newborns/kids, was minimal at best.

title: Not what I had hoped for
body:
It’s taken me a while to write this review (I did the course about 12 months ago now). I think because I part of me felt let down and disappointed and the other part felt embarrassed to have been influenced into this course when I could have saved money and learnt more doing a smaller, locally run class. 

Overall the instructor was very knowledgeable, however unfortunately the class size was just too large to actually make it worthwhile. She also had wey to much content to cover within the time frame. 

A large portion of the course was spent on cpr which I did not find beneficial as do annual basic life support for infants/children st work. I do understand that this is important to cover for most though, however feel it displaced and made the actual content I wanted covered (eg fever, febrile convulsions, falls first aid) feel rushed, incomplete and I can’t recall most of it. I also was not impressed at the quality of videos (all snippets sent in by parents on social media).

Thank you for taking the time to share your experience with us. We are sorry to hear that our Brisbane Public Course did not meet your expectations when you attended. We understand your disappointment and want to apologise, we certainly dont want anyone to walk away from the course feeling this way.

We appreciate your feedback as it helps us ensure that we remain the leading provider in this space. As your course was over 12 months ago, we do want to let you know that we have made significant improvements to our courses and presentations delivered in the classroom.

We would love to help in rectifying the situation and making sure that you receive the information you were looking for. We believe that our core mission is to provide valuable and practical knowledge to our customers, and if we have failed to do so, we apologise.

Please expect an email from us soon, as we would love to discuss this further and assist you in any way we can. Thank you again for your feedback, and we hope to have the opportunity to make it up to you.

Tiny Hearts Team

title: 5 Stars
body:
We are expecting our first child and had Tiny Hearts attended our home for Baby and Child First Aid  to teach my partner and I and our immediate families the knowledge and skills that are required to keep our soon to arrive baby safe . Hands down the best thing we have done, whilst we hope not to even need to use the knowledge and tools learnt over the weekend, not only do we as parents feel confident and reassured that we have the knowledge and tools to use in a range of situations, but also confidence that our loved ones have the same information and tools when looking after or around our baby; and importantly they too feel the same. 
The educator who ran our private workshop was wonderful. He was incredibly knowledgeable and engaging. To have 10 people engaged, learning and retaining information for the entire 4 hours is incredible. Four days later and everyone is still saying how much they got out of the course and how happy they are that we organised the private workshop. 

For anyone thinking about it, it’s a no brainer.  Book in the private course and gather your nearest and dearest. You will not regret it.

title: Dangerous Product with concern
body:
On three occasions now your thermometer has now come not even close to appropriately registering fever in my child.

All three occasions, this thermometer has read 36.7 (both using the ear and forehead) or below when in fact my child has had a fever of 38.0 and above, even a fever of 39.8 at it’s peak and the thermometer still read below 36.7.

The lense is not dirty and the product has been stored appropriately since purchase. 

Very unsafe. Would not recommend as a trained medical professional.

The Tiny Hearts Team

title: Inaccurate Readings
body: I wanted to love this thermometer, it sounded so great and so foolproof/easy to use but unfortunately I haven’t been able to rely on its accuracy. It gives different readings for each ear & for the forehead & is out I think up to .5 of a degree. We have switched back to our old one which provides a more consistent result.
reply:
Hi Sarah,

Firstly, thank you for supporting Tiny Hearts, I am sad that this product hasn't met your expectations but I am positive we can assist you with some tips on how to position to get reliable readings; I have sent you an email. Just also wanted to note it's normal to get different readings in each ear, in order to track a temperature correctly you want to use the same ear each reading, rather than switching ears. Our thermometers are tested to be within +0.3 degrees celsius. The way infrared technology works is the sensor will collect infrared energy emitted by the ear drum, which is why the position of the probe is imperative. Depending on age, you might pull the ear straight back or back and upwards at the same time. We look forward to hearing from you so we can help you achieve accurate and reliable readings each time. 

Kindest, 
Tiny Hearts

title: Too short, not enough details

It is a good starter for someone who does not know anything about first aid. Unfortunately most sections do not have enough information about the topic for our taste. It's just some generic tips that you can find with a quick google search. This pattern continues throughout the course, short videos without visuals and detailed information. On top of that the website is slow and the intro music is annoying. Wanna hear the same, 10 second clip of generic electronic music every two minutes when you start a new  session? No, me neither. Besides, it doesn't fit the topic. First aid is not a hip lifestyle topic, I find it rather serious.

My wife said the videos are essentially the same as the ones you can find on instagram. So, not worth the money.

title: Overall great course, but some modifications needed
body: We registered for this course as it was the most extensive out of the ones available in Adelaide and covered the most topics. Overall it was great, the instructor was very knowledgeable and the information was useful. However, the allocation of time between topics should be revisited - for example, most attendees indicated they were interested in learning about choking and yet this topic was rushed through at the end, while less important topics (e.g. pain relief) were allocated far too much time in my opinion. Also, it might be worth reinforcing in your reminder emails that if people are unwell they should stay at home - we were in a fairly crowded room with multiple people who were clearly unwell, which is quite distressing with so many pregnant women present.

title: Awesome Content
body:
Mighty glad I was able to attend as an Interpreter for JoAnne Ward & Linda Flesser, as I too was able to learn some very valuable details about the advised CPR strategies & reminders of how some unpredictable incidents can occur and having a plan to execute when circumstances call for it, is definitely worth the consideration. Safety and minimal risk practices can be applied, now that I've gained that insight - its priceless, truly!
VERY grateful to be able to provide Interpreting for families, that may otherwise have to go without being across this kind of content, that's surely invaluable to any parent/family setting!
I'm a strong believer in; ''When you know better, you do better" - so biggest Thankyou again to the Team for allowing us to know better, for the benefit of our children, and role modelling what attentive and conscious parenting truly looks like!

title: Good Course

Good course that covers range of hazards. I left feeling more confident that I had a baseline level of knowledge should I need it. Many of the lessons very practical. 

The thing that would make it 5 stars would be: 1) more explanation of “why” certain protocols. (Eg not just no tweezers to remove stings, tell us the reason why no tweezers as this will help me understand better to apply the principle) 2) it would have been helpful to receive a workbook for the course in person so I could take notes. But I’m sure the online reference guide will help anyways

title: Parenting Essential!
body:
I did the online course, it was super easy to follow and extremely informative. Even without the "physical" component of a face to face class, I felt confident in my skills.
 
I was in the unfortunate situation shortly after completing the course where I needed to use the skills and performed CPR on my 7wk old bubba. It came like second nature, despite the terror I knew exactly what to do,  was calm and able to keep him going until the ambos arrived. I have no doubt that my little boy is here and completely okay because of this training.

I hope no parent ever has to use it but I can't stress enough how important it is. Your response in an emergency absolutely dictates the outcome and while no one ever thinks it will happen to them, make sure you have the skills to provide the best emergency care for your little one.

title: First Aid Kit
body:
Overall, I was very impressed with the kit. Please note that the below items are minor, and wouldn’t change my mind about purchasing again. 

Just a couple of things that I didn’t expect. I had thought that the kit would be secured with a latch to make it more challenging for the child prying fingers to access the kit. 

Also, the font of the text on the individual kit items can make it difficult to read what it is, quickly and fast. I imagine in an event, it may be a little frustrating for the flustered novice (that I am) to figure out which one I am looking for quickly. 

Again, I am impressed with the overall item and definitely agree that it is one of the best fitted out as well as good looking kits on the market.
